name: ConvBoost Exit Rescue
author: numeriweb

sections.description:
ConvBoost Exit Rescue helps you reduce mobile bounces by catching a key “exit moment”: when a visitor uses the back button or back gesture to leave.

Instead of losing that visitor immediately, you can redirect them to a chosen Rescue Page (for example: your best offer, a discount page, a lead magnet, a product category, or a contact page). This creates a simple, lightweight exit intent experience designed for mobile behavior.

It’s built to stay simple, clear, and lightweight: set it up in minutes, keep the output minimal, and avoid heavy popups or page builders.

Why users choose ConvBoost

Many “exit intent popup” plugins focus on desktop mouse-leave events. On mobile, people often exit by swiping back.
ConvBoost Exit Rescue is designed specifically to help with:
* Mobile bounce prevention
* Better retention and more second pageviews
* Redirecting to key pages to increase leads and sales

Features

  • Mobile-first “exit intent” rescue based on the back button / back gesture
  • Choose a Rescue Page to redirect visitors to (offers, collections, lead pages, etc.)
  • Designed to be user-friendly (avoids overly aggressive behavior)
  • Helps improve:
    • Pageviews and time on site
    • Lead capture and newsletter signups
    • Conversion rate optimization (CRO)
    • Cart abandonment recovery (especially for WooCommerce stores)

Common use cases

  • Redirect bounces to a discount / coupon page
  • Send visitors to “Best sellers” or a key product category
  • Show a “Before you go” lead magnet (PDF, checklist, free guide)
  • Route visitors to support / contact to reduce lost leads
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. Go to ConvBoost Exit Rescue and select your Rescue Page
sections.faq:
What is “Exit intent” on mobile?

On mobile, “exit intent” is usually triggered by a visitor leaving via the back button or back gesture. Exit Rescue is designed for that behavior.

Does it work on mobile?

Yes. It is designed for mobile back button / gesture exits.

Are there any restrictions?

Overly aggressive configurations are not allowed by the plugin so it stays user friendly.

Does it interrupt normal browsing?

By default, it only arms on the first page a visitor sees, so it prevents hard bounces without hijacking navigation between pages.

Can I use it with WooCommerce?

Yes. Many store owners use it as a lightweight cart abandonment helper by redirecting exits to an offer page, category page, or support page.
